focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	I run product for a nine-person software company.
e002	One of our oldest customers, Northline, wants a reporting workspace that is quite different from what we planned this quarter.
e003	They are not threatening to leave, but their operations lead keeps saying it would make the product usable across the rest of their team.
e004	Meanwhile we have reliability work we have postponed twice, and we told smaller customers that the next release would simplify the core workflow.
e005	I keep moving between “this is how good products learn” and “we are letting the loudest customer set the roadmap.”
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e006	The immediate distinction is whether Northline is revealing a broader need or buying influence over a small team.
e007	I would not decide from the size of the account alone.
e008	Ask what exact job the workspace enables, what they do today, and which parts could serve other customers.
e009	In parallel, make the reliability and roadmap cost visible.
e010	If the request consumes the same people who own those commitments, “we can probably fit it in” is already a choice to delay them.
[Turn 7 USER]
e060	My provisional plan is to offer Northline three focused sessions over the next two weeks, document the workflow, and explicitly make no build commitment.
e061	Lina can lead the sessions but not start production code.
e062	In the same period we will define the reliability work and the core-workflow release we are actually willing to promise.
e063	Then we decide with all three pieces visible.
e064	I still worry that “no production code” wastes Lina's best way of learning and that Northline will hear a polite no.
e065	But starting the build now feels less defensible than it did.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e066	That plan protects the learning opportunity without pretending the underlying tradeoff is resolved.
e067	The two risks you named remain real: restricting prototypes may make discovery artificial, while careful language may still feel like distance to Northline.
e068	You can decide in advance what kind of disposable prototype is allowed and ask Northline to reflect back what they believe the sessions mean.
e069	Neither step guarantees trust or a good product decision, but both make misunderstanding easier to notice before momentum chooses for you.
